summary: Working in Tibetology and Indology, Richard B. Martin was a professor (attested 1983–1991) and South Asian bibliographer (attested 2003) at the University of Virginia.

Richard Baker, working in Buddhist and religious studies, studied under Shunryu Suzuki in 1961 and at UC Berkeley, Harvard, Wisconsin-Madison, Minnesota, and Colorado Boulder. He founded the San Francisco Zen Center, serving as abbot from 1971 to 1984.

Richard Barron is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teachers Kalu Rinpoche, Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima, and the 3rd Jamgon Kongtrul Lodro Chokyi Senge.

Richard Bertram Whitehead was an Indologist and historian who studied at Exeter College, Oxford, and Cambridge (D.Litt., 1940). He co-founded the Numismatic Society of India (1910) and was a Fellow-Commoner at St John's College from 1922.

A scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies, Richard Bowring earned his BA, doctorate, and Litt.D. at Cambridge. He taught at Columbia and Princeton before becoming Professor (1985) and Selwyn College Master (2000–2012) at Cambridge.

Richard Burghart worked in Indology and religious studies, earning degrees at Williams College and SOAS. He taught Asian anthropology at the London School of Economics (1977–1979) and SOAS (1979–1988), and was Professor of Anthropology at Heidelberg University from 1988.
Richard Burn was an Indologist and historian who studied at Christ Church, Oxford (1889–1893). He co-founded the Numismatic Society of India and served in the Indian Civil Service from 1893 to 1927.

Richard Carnac Temple was an Indology and history scholar who studied at Trinity Hall, Cambridge. He served in the Bengal and Indian Staff Corps, edited the Indian Antiquary (1885–1931), and founded Panjab Notes and Queries (1883).

Richard Constant Boer was a linguist and Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Groningen in 1888. He served as Privatdozent at Groningen (1888–1900) and Professor of Old Germanic and Sanskrit at Amsterdam (1900–1929).
Working in Indology and religious studies, Richard D. Mann completed his PhD at McMaster University under Phyllis Granoff (attested 2003) and held a post at Carleton University (attested 2007).

Specializing in Buddhist studies and sinology, Richard D. McBride II completed his PhD at UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr. He held posts at Washington University in St. Louis, Dongguk University, and Brigham Young University.

Richard De Smet was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Michel Ledrus and Robert Antoine, completing his Ph.D. at the Pontifical Gregorian University. From 1954, he served as Professor of Indian Philosophy at De Nobili College.

Richard Delbrück was an archaeologist who earned his Ph.D. at Bonn (1899). He served as Director of the German Archaeological Institute at Rome (1911–1915) and held professorships at the universities of Jena, Giessen (1922–1928), and Bonn (1928–1940).

Richard F. Nance is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies who earned his AM and PhD at the University of Chicago. He taught at Chicago, Wisconsin-Madison, and was Assistant Professor at Indiana University Bloomington (2013–2021).

Richard Fick was an Indologist who completed his Ph.D. at Kiel University under Richard Pischel. He worked at the Prussian State Library, became director of the Göttingen State and University Library (1921–1932), and was an honorary professor at Göttingen.

id: P:Richard Fleming St. Andrew St. John
summary: Richard Fleming St. Andrew St. John studied at Wadham College, Oxford, working in linguistics and Indology. He taught Burmese at University College London (1894) and served as Teacher of Hindūstânî at Oxford from 1890 to 1910.

Richard Foltz, working in Iranian and Central Asian studies and history, completed his MA at Utah and PhD at Harvard. He taught at Florida and has been a professor and Centre for Iranian Studies director at Concordia University since 2005.
Richard Francis Burton was an Indologist and scholar of religious studies who studied at Trinity College, Oxford, in 1840. He was the founder of the Kama Shastra Society.

Richard Fritzsche was an Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Leipzig (1869–1873), studying under Hermann Brockhaus, Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl, and Georg Curtius. He later served as Rektor at Gymnasium Schneeberg (1888–1916).

Richard G. Salomon is an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and linguist who studied under Ludo Rocher. He served as Professor and later Professor Emeritus of Sanskrit at the University of Washington from 1981 to 2020.
